why_this_case: Separates a responder that reads 'B2B SaaS' and emits the PLG playbook — self-serve signup telemetry, checkout and payment-method events, marketplace listing behaviour — from one that reads the actual site: a demo-only CTA, a pricing page that is a quote-request form, an AWS Marketplace listing that is private-offer-only, and an agentless architecture whose defining pre-contract signal is a cloud access grant. It also forces the off-website and post-sale families (F09 implementation prep, F13 operational/regulatory triggers, F14 buying group, F15 competitor/incident) that unaided answers miss, and it makes the security-vendor trap explicit: entity-level breach disclosure is a signal, person-level breach-victim lists are a prohibition.

b2b_b2c.why: Every customer named on the homepage and customers page is an enterprise (Morgan Stanley, Siemens, BMW, Salesforce, LVMH, ServiceNow, Fox, Colgate-Palmolive); testimonials are attributed to CISOs, Deputy CISOs and VPs of Cybersecurity Operations. No consumer offer exists anywhere on the site.

business_model.why: Pricing page describes licences that scale 'with your workloads, active developers, log ingestion, or sensors' — a metered multi-year subscription. Three product lines (Wiz Cloud, Wiz Code, Wiz Defend) sold as platform modules.

sales_motion.why: The only primary CTA on the site is 'Get a demo'. The header auth link is 'Sign in', never 'Sign up'. /pricing is a lead form headed 'Pricing request' offering a 'custom quote' with no published prices. 'hybrid' is defensible because of the Partner Alliance resell/services tracks and a partner portal at partners.wiz.io with an application flow. 'self_serve' is wrong.

has_self_serve_signup.why: No unattended, card-self-serve provisioning: the only nav CTAs are 'Get a demo' and 'Sign in', /pricing is a 'Pricing request' form with no published number, and the AWS Marketplace listing is titled 'Wiz [Private Offer Only]'. Two form-gated pre-purchase routes DO exist and were missed on first capture: /free-trial (HTTP 200, 'Start your free trial of Wiz', 14-day unlimited access) and /preview (emails a link to a preview environment). Both require work email, phone, job title and company, and neither is linked from the homepage nav or /pricing - grep count 0 for 'free-trial' in both. So accept false or null: a tool that finds the unlinked trial page and answers null is being more accurate than one that asserts no trial exists.

purchase_motion.why: Custom-quoted platform licence sold to Fortune 100 security organisations; the pricing page refuses to publish a number at all.

consideration.why: Gated Customer Trust Center carrying ISO 27001/27017/27018/27701, SOC 2 Type II + HIPAA, SOC 3 and PCI DSS v4.0.1 AoC/RoC; analyst positioning (Forrester Wave, IDC MarketScape) surfaced on the homepage. These artefacts exist to satisfy a security and procurement review, which only high-consideration purchases run.

purchase_cycle.why: Demo -> POV against the customer's own cloud -> security/procurement review -> custom quote. 'long' is the modal case at Fortune-100 scale; 'medium' is defensible for mid-market. 'short' is wrong.

consumable_vs_durable.why: A term licence to a platform, not a consumable that depletes. Nothing is used up and reordered.

requires_plg_motion.why: No self-serve product access exists before contract, so there is no pre-purchase product-usage surface to instrument. This is the single most load-bearing profile fact in the case.

has_review_site_category.why: The customers page carries a '826 Reviews | 4.7' badge plus 4.8 and 4.4 ratings, and the homepage cites Forrester Wave and IDC MarketScape leadership. Cloud security / CNAPP is a well-populated review and analyst category. A responder that says 'no review-site category, skip review signals' is wrong here.

dev_audience.why: Wiz Code is described as securing development 'from IDE to CI/CD'; the integrations directory lists 20 CI/CD integrations (GitHub, GitLab, Jenkins, AWS CodeBuild) and 9 Kubernetes integrations; the Zendesk quote is 'Wiz gives us a common language between security and engineering'. Developers are users even though the CISO is the economic buyer.

has_owned_community.why: The footer offers blog, courses, customer stories, newsroom and events, but no public forum or user community is linked. Either 'false' or 'not determinable from the site' is acceptable; 'true' is not.

industry.why: Cloud and AI security platform (Wiz Cloud / Wiz Code / Wiz Defend). Matches the industry_boost vocabularies used across F13 and F15 entries.

has_physical_fulfilment.why: Agentless SaaS with 310+ software integrations. Nothing is shipped, delivered, installed on a site, or surveyed. No store locator, no delivery language, no field-service function anywhere on the site.

must_include_signals.why: /pricing is literally a 'Pricing request' form producing a 'custom quote' — the pricing surface IS the request event. The form fields (product interest, cloud estate) name the configuration a seller must price.
'Get a demo' is the sole primary CTA sitewide and the only path into the funnel. The held/no-show/rescheduled outcome is the first real commitment measure available on this shape.

The observable form here is a security or procurement questionnaire issued to a supplier set, an RFP invitation, or a named-competitor answer on the demo form. Strength 5 and the point at which Wiz learns it is in a bake-off against Prisma Cloud, Orca or Microsoft Defender for Cloud rather than selling unopposed.

The Customer Trust Center is gated ('Explore our Customer Trust Center'), so a request for the SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 certificate or PCI DSS v4.0.1 AoC is a named, attributable, timestamped event rather than an anonymous download. On this shape the risk-class asset request is a mid-to-late stage signal, not a browsing artefact.

Anti-overcorrection. The catalogue entry explicitly covers 'a sales-provisioned pilot or proof of concept', which is exactly how a Wiz POV runs. A responder that reasons 'no self-serve trial, therefore no trial signal' has over-corrected; the signal exists, its provisioning is sales-mediated, and its identity level is account.

Multi-year metered licences with notice periods. The company's own book of term_end dates is the highest-strength (5) post-sale signal available and needs no new instrumentation — it is already in the contract record.

The named roles on the customers page — CISO, Deputy CISO, VP Cybersecurity Operations, Director of Product Security, CTO — are different people in one account. Two or more distinct people from one organisation touching the same evaluation inside a window is the transition from curiosity to a funded evaluation on this shape.

A target posting for a Cloud Security Engineer, Kubernetes platform engineer or a first CISO is a public, cost-free declaration that the buyer is standing up the function Wiz serves. Available now from public postings with no first-party dependency at all.

The customer logo wall includes scale-ups (Lovable, Wolt) alongside the Fortune 100. A funding round is a dated, publicly recorded budget opening that precedes both cloud-estate growth and the first security hire, and it is an account-level fact with no person-level inference in it.

The highest-value pre-contract signal on this specific company and the one most likely to be missed. Wiz is agentless: a POV cannot begin until the prospect grants a scoped cloud role into their AWS/Azure/GCP account. That grant is internally expensive, requires the cloud platform team rather than the champion, and carries a scope, a grant timestamp and a revocation state. Strength 5, permission explicit_consent.

F09 is the family unaided answers skip. The pre-contract half is what matters here: connector configuration against a second cloud account, a test policy import, opening a migration ticket off the incumbent, naming an internal project owner, or requesting an implementation scope call. The catalogue entry deliberately spans both sides of the sale, so the same fields also detect a stalled onboarding after close.

The valuable half is the absence: a closed enterprise account with no kickoff booked N business days after signature is a stalled deployment, and on a platform priced per workload a stalled deployment caps the expansion the contract was underwritten on. Export from CRM plus calendar; no new instrumentation.

Strength 5 and structurally guaranteed on this shape: a Fortune 100 security purchase produces a vendor security questionnaire, a DPA, a certificate of insurance, supplier onboarding forms and a PO number. Each artefact exists only to authorise the purchase internally, and each carries a date that gates the close.

The Partner Alliance runs an explicit 'Services' track, and CNAPP selection at this scale routinely passes through a GSI, an MSSP or a Gartner analyst inquiry. The decision may be made by a firm Wiz is not talking to. Strength 5 and almost universally absent from unaided answers.

The partner portal at partners.wiz.io implies deal registration, and the AWS Marketplace route is private-offer-only, i.e. every marketplace transaction arrives attached to a named partner or seller record. That is a resolvable referrer, not a channel bucket — and it is where the marketplace signal actually lives on this shape.

The compliance solution page names PCI, GDPR, HIPAA, NIST, CIS, HiTrust and SOC 2 and claims 100+ built-in frameworks. The signal is not the rule but the join: a dated obligation plus the account attributes that put a specific prospect in its scope test. Requires a maintained obligation table and an account attribute join — a genuine capability build, not a pixel.

Wiz replaces an incumbent. Two dated observations of a target's publicly observable stack differing on a named component — a new cloud provider, a new Kubernetes distribution, a dropped competing scanner — is the switch window. The 310+ integration directory is the join table for which components matter.

Licences scale with workloads, active developers, log ingestion and sensors, so an account whose scanned estate is approaching its contracted entitlement before term end has a dated expansion trigger. The entry requires a contract end date and a trailing growth rate, so the output is a date rather than a ratio — and it is permission contractual_access, not tracking.

A dated, public degradation at a named competitor — an end-of-life notice, a tier restructure, an acquisition, a repeated outage — joined to first-party records of which accounts and lost deals run that provider. Cloud security has had exactly these events, and the join to lost-deal records is the part that makes it a signal rather than news.

The category-native trigger and the one that must be handled correctly. A publicly disclosed breach, an exploited CVE in a named product and version range, or a lapsed certification at a provider a target depends on, joined to first-party records of which accounts run it. Entity-level and public only — see must_flag_restricted.

Strength 5 and specific to the displacement motion: a prospect exporting policy or findings from an incumbent CNAPP, standing a Wiz environment beside a live one, or sitting in switching documentation. Post-sale the same fields read as a churn warning when a Wiz customer does it in the other direction.

The correct F08 member for this shape and the discrimination against f08.payment_preparation. There is no checkout, but there is a purchase-order reference, a cost-centre code, a tax registration number and an invoicing contact — billing-only fields that exist solely to invoice somebody, and that only get completed once the purchase is internally decided. Strength 5.

The integrations directory — 310+ integrations across 35+ categories, named systems like ServiceNow, Splunk, Jira, Okta, EKS/GKE/AKS/OpenShift — is a fitment surface. A prospect looking up whether their specific SIEM or ticketing system is supported executes an integration lookup carrying an identifier of the incumbent thing and receives a pass/fail. Website-instrumentation availability, and almost always missed because it does not look like a buying page.

must_exclude_signals.why: f08.account_verification is the only catalogue row carrying applicability.requires_plg_motion = true, and its consumable_vs_durable is ['consumable']; Wiz meets neither. The original grounding - 'no account exists pre-contract' - was factually wrong: a sales-gated 14-day trial at /free-trial does provision a pre-contract tenant. The exclusion survives on the narrower and correct basis that there is no unattended signup funnel to instrument, only a lead form a human qualifies.
must_exclude_signals.failure_mode: the PLG playbook imported on the words 'B2B SaaS' - emitting signup-funnel telemetry for a company whose only pre-purchase route is a human-qualified lead form

must_exclude_signals.why: There is no checkout, no card capture and no wallet handshake anywhere in this motion; the entry's own applicability lists sales_motion self_serve and hybrid only. Wiz is paid by invoice against a PO or through an AWS Marketplace private offer, both of which are settled after signature, not during evaluation.
must_exclude_signals.failure_mode: Cart-and-checkout thinking applied to an enterprise contract. A responder that recommends both f08.payment_preparation and f08.billing_setup has not distinguished a payment instrument from an invoicing artefact, which is exactly the distinction that survives here.

must_exclude_signals.why: The subtle trap. Wiz IS on AWS Marketplace, so 'monitor marketplace demand signals' looks correct — but the listing is 'Wiz [Private Offer Only]' with pricing routed to marketplace@wiz.io. There is no public listing to browse, no cart-add, no watch, no buyer question, and no shopper telemetry of any kind. The entry describes ecommerce/marketplace listing demand (business_model ecommerce, marketplace; sales_motion self_serve, hybrid), which is not what a private-offer transaction is.
must_exclude_signals.failure_mode: Seeing a marketplace listing and inferring marketplace shopper behaviour. The correct marketplace-adjacent signal on this shape is f14.referral_source_named on the private offer or deal registration.

must_exclude_signals.why: Catches F09 family shotgunning. F09 IS expected here — but only the software half. Wiz is agentless; there is no fitting, commissioning, pre-install survey, service location or installer network. The entry requires a service_location_id and an install-class job type, neither of which exists.
must_exclude_signals.failure_mode: Answering the family rather than the company: recognising that F09 is relevant and then emitting all four members, including the two that require a physical site.

must_exclude_signals.why: Nothing ships. No delivery window, no delivery address, no slot selection, no serviceability check against an address, no removal of the item being replaced. The entry keys on a fulfilment record with a promised delivery window at transaction identity level.
must_exclude_signals.failure_mode: Same F09 shotgun as above, plus the deeper error of assuming an enterprise purchase has physical fulfilment because it has an implementation.

must_exclude_signals.why: The entry applies to consumables only and says so explicitly: 'projecting a depletion date for a durable is a category error'. A metered software licence renews on a contract date; it does not deplete and get reordered. The correct member is f11.subscription_renewal_window, which is in must_include.
must_exclude_signals.failure_mode: Conflating renewal with replenishment — treating a term-end date as a depletion projection. Also catches the reverse: a responder that emits replenishment because per-workload metering superficially resembles consumption.

must_exclude_signals.why: Identity level household, keyed on at least three transactions across two inter-purchase intervals in a retail rhythm. Enterprise accounts transact once or twice a year against a negotiated agreement; there is no cadence to compute and the identity unit is an account, not a household.
must_exclude_signals.failure_mode: An identity-level error — attaching a household-keyed retail signal to a B2B account. The README records that 0 of 7 unaided runs assigned an identity level at all, so this exclusion tests exactly the field that goes missing.

must_exclude_signals.why: The entry carries applicability.industry_exclude = ['software'] and identity level location. Construction, planning and trade permits attach to a site address or parcel; a cloud security platform has neither a site nor a permit-gated purchase.
must_exclude_signals.failure_mode: F13 family shotgunning. A responder that correctly identifies F13 as the discriminating family and then emits all eight members has learned the taxonomy but not read the company.

must_exclude_signals.why: F12 is not applicable to this company at all. The entry needs a date the person supplied for a stated purpose (a birthday reminder, a need-it-by date) at individual identity with explicit consent, in an ecommerce/marketplace/services model. Nothing on wiz.io collects a personal occasion date.
must_exclude_signals.failure_mode: Reaching for a consumer calendar to explain B2B timing — typically by mis-mapping 'fiscal year end' or 'budget flush' onto a personal occasion trigger. The lawful B2B forms of dated timing are f13.regulatory_compliance_deadline, f11.subscription_renewal_window and f06.budget_allocation.

must_exclude_signals.why: Requires a return or exchange record joined to an order, in an ecommerce/marketplace/subscription model with variant SKUs. A cancelled or downgraded enterprise licence produces no return record and no RMA; the correct signal for a customer walking away from an incumbent is f01.alternative_solution_abandonment, and for their own deterioration f10.service_deterioration.
must_exclude_signals.failure_mode: Mapping SaaS downgrade or non-renewal onto a returns artefact that does not exist, which then produces a recommendation to instrument a system the company does not run.

families_not_applicable.why: Personal, household and occasion triggers. Every member of F12 keys on a natural person's declared personal circumstance — relocation, wedding, trip dates, academic enrolment, care episode, household consumption at a delivery address, gift purchase, personal occasion date. Wiz sells a metered cloud security platform to enterprise security organisations; there is no consumer, no household, no delivery address and no personal calendar anywhere in the motion. A responder that emits any F12 member here is pattern-matching on 'timing' rather than on the buyer.

must_flag_restricted.why: The defining temptation for a security vendor and the one a naive answer reaches for first: assemble a list of people named in credential dumps, leak-site postings or a breach notification register and market a remedy to them, or attach an 'exposed' attribute to records already held. The catalogue names the lawful alternative precisely — entity-level public disclosure joined to first-party account records, which is f15.security_incident in must_include. The pair is the whole point of the case: the same news event yields a permitted account-level signal and a prohibited person-level list, and a tool that scores rather than gates will emit the second.

Wiz's product is a standing read role into a customer's cloud environment, granted to evaluate or run the platform. The technical capability to mine that scan output for attributes the customer never granted it for — their other vendors, their internal org shape, third parties whose data sits inside the connected stores — already exists the moment the token works. This is the class the README describes as separated from unlawfulness by nothing except restraint, and it must appear as a do-not-collect entry alongside f07.consent_and_access_granting rather than as a low-scoring signal.

The flipside of f13.funding_or_capital_event. Wiz sells to venture-backed scale-ups (Lovable, Wolt appear on the logo wall) whose directors and founders are natural persons with purchasable credit-header, judgment and insolvency records. Deriving that a named director is in financial difficulty in order to time, price or route an approach sits outside any FCRA permissible purpose. The lawful variant is the entity-level fact only — a company's own published insolvency or administration notice — with no inference about any person behind it.

expected_capability_notes: There is no unattended card-self-serve provisioning and no public tracking surface that produces product usage. The pre-purchase product surface is a sales-gated 14-day free trial (/free-trial) and an emailed preview environment (/preview), both form-gated and unlinked from the nav. So product-usage and capacity signals are not UNAVAILABLE outright - they are available only post-provisioning, on a tenant the seller controls, and should be reported that way rather than as a self-serve telemetry stream.

f07.trial is still available despite the absence of a self-serve trial, because the catalogue entry covers a sales-provisioned pilot or proof of concept. A tool that marks all trial signals unavailable has over-corrected; the right answer keeps the signal and changes its source_class from product_analytics to CRM/first_party_backend.

The AWS Marketplace listing is 'Private Offer Only'. A marketplace channel exists, but it produces no public shopper telemetry — the observable artefact is a private-offer or deal-registration record arriving through a partner feed, which is f14.referral_source_named, not f04.marketplace_activity.

docs.wiz.io returned HTTP 403 to unauthenticated fetch at capture time. Documentation-depth signals (f04.information_depth_escalation, and the documentation half of f09.implementation_preparation) are real but observable only through Wiz's own instrumentation on a gated property. They must be reported as first-party instrumentation on an authenticated surface, with an availability of website_instrumentation or integration, never as public-web observation.

The Customer Trust Center is gated behind a request. That makes f04.risk_reduction_behavior stronger here than on a company that publishes its SOC 2 openly: the artefact request is attributable to a named person and account rather than being an anonymous PDF download, so its identity_level should be reported as account or individual, not visitor.

f07.consent_and_access_granting is the highest-value pre-contract signal on this shape because the agentless architecture makes a cloud role grant a precondition of evaluation. It must be reported with permission_requirement explicit_consent, identity_level account, and a revocation state — a grant that has since been revoked is the opposite signal.

Every website-observed signal on this case (F02 members, f04.risk_reduction_behavior, f04.information_depth_escalation, f05.compatibility_check, f06.roi_analysis) carries availability website_instrumentation and permission_requirement of at least notice. Wiz serves EEA and UK visitors from a single global site, so non-essential terminal-equipment access needs consent there. A tool that reports any of these as 'available now, permission none' has collapsed the availability and permission axes — the exact failure the catalogue's two-field split exists to prevent.

The F14 signals are CRM-resident and depend on a field the company must first choose to capture. f14.stakeholder_role_coverage is unavailable, not merely weak, if contact_role is not recorded against the opportunity; its capability ladder therefore starts at 'record roles on contacts', not at 'score coverage'. Reporting it as available now without that prerequisite is a conflation of relevant with obtainable.

f13.regulatory_compliance_deadline is not satisfied by a list of regulations. The entry requires both halves: a dated obligation AND account attributes matching that obligation's scope test (jurisdiction, sector, size band, data processed). A tool that returns 'track DORA and NIS2 deadlines' without the account-attribute join has returned news, not a signal.

Wiz became a Google Cloud subsidiary on 11 March 2026 while retaining its brand, site and multi-cloud positioning. Any parent-company channel effect belongs in f14.referral_source_named and f14.advisor_involvement; it does not change the profile, and a tool that reclassifies the business shape on the strength of the acquisition is wrong.
notes:
CAPTURE CONDITIONS. www.wiz.io, /pricing, /partners, /integrations, /careers, /customers, /solutions/compliance and /trust-center all returned readable HTML on 2026-08-01. docs.wiz.io returned HTTP 403 to unauthenticated fetch — treated as a deliberate degraded-capture condition and reflected in expected_capability_notes rather than guessed around. The AWS Marketplace listing title 'Wiz [Private Offer Only]' was verified off-site; it is load-bearing for the f04.marketplace_activity exclusion, so a scorer rejecting that exclusion should check the listing rather than the wiz.io site.

STABILITY CAVEAT. Google completed its acquisition of Wiz on 11 March 2026 and stated Wiz would keep its brand and multi-cloud commitment. At capture time wiz.io is independently branded with its own demo CTA, pricing-request form and partner portal. If the site later redirects into cloud.google.com properties, re-capture rather than re-score: the profile fields most likely to move are sales_motion (deeper hybrid via Google Cloud field sales) and the marketplace route (a Google Cloud Marketplace listing would change the f04.marketplace_activity verdict).

FAMILY COVERAGE VS REQUIRED SIGNALS. families_expected lists 14 families, but must_include_signals names members of only 11 of them. F01, F02 and F03 are expected as families and deliberately carry no required member: their applicable signals are listed under ACCEPTABLE below, and any one of them satisfies the family. Score family coverage against families_expected and signal recall against must_include_signals; do not treat the three-family gap as an error in either direction.

ACCEPTABLE, DO NOT PENALISE. These are defensible for this company and should be marked neither wrong nor missing: f01.explicit_need_statement, f01.alternative_solution_abandonment, f01.operational_problem_reported, f02.search_query, f03.content_consumption, f03.conference_activity, f03.webinar_attendance, f03.review_reading, f04.product_comparison, f04.information_depth_escalation, f05.requirement_formation, f05.diagnostic_tool_use, f06.roi_analysis, f06.budget_allocation, f06.negotiation, f07.consultation, f07.time_investment_escalation, f10.product_usage, f10.service_deterioration, f11.upgrade_cycle_due, f13.rfp_or_tender_issued, f14.stakeholder_role_coverage, f15.policy_incentive_change. Several of these are strong; they are out of must_include only to keep the required set to signals whose evidence is visible on the site itself.

JUDGEMENT CALLS MADE EXPLICIT. (1) f03.review_reading: the customers page carries a '826 Reviews | 4.7' badge but does not name its source, and it is not clear whether the widget is instrumented. The category plainly exists, so 'no review-site category' is wrong, but requiring the signal would be unfair. (2) f15.policy_incentive_change overlaps f13.regulatory_compliance_deadline; the F13 member is required because it demands the account-attribute join, and the F15 member is accepted as an alternative reading rather than a duplicate. (3) has_owned_community could not be determined: the footer offers courses and events but links no forum, so both false and null are accepted. (4) consideration accepts only 'high' — for a custom-quoted Fortune-100 platform purchase behind a gated trust center, 'medium' is not defensible.

CATALOGUE COVERAGE FINDING. f07.seller_inventory_allocation fits this company well — the pricing page produces a human-priced custom quote, and a POV consumes a named solutions architect, both of which the definition covers exactly ('a quote priced by a human rather than a calculator', 'a specialist or engineer assigned'). It was left out of must_include because its applicability.business_model is ['services','marketplace','ecommerce','subscription'] and omits 'saas', so a filter honouring applicability would not surface it for a SaaS profile. If that omission is an authoring gap rather than a deliberate scope decision, adding 'saas' would make the entry fire on exactly the sales-led enterprise SaaS shape it describes best. CORRECTION 2026-08-01: an adversarial pass found https://www.wiz.io/free-trial returns HTTP 200 with a 14-day trial offer, falsifying this case's original claim that no trial exists anywhere on wiz.io. The affected profile field, capability note and exclusion rationale have been re-grounded on what is actually unobservable (no unattended signup funnel) rather than on a false absence.
